chunks.title: Acquired cataract
chunks.tldr: Slow blur, glare (headlights), colour dulling. Nuclear: myopic shift (second sight), distance worse. PSC: young, steroids/diabetes/uveitis/radiation, glare + reading trouble, better when dilated. Cortical: spokes, glare. Special: Christmas tree (myotonic), sunflower (Wilson), snowflake (juvenile diabetes), Vossius ring (trauma), glaukomflecken, atopic (anterior subcapsular), NF2 (PSC). Cataract never causes RAPD.
points: Ask about tamsulosin (floppy iris).
Pre-op: dilation, density, PXF, phacodonesis, guttae; biometry (K + axial length); B-scan if no view.
PAM/interferometry overestimate potential in macular holes/amblyopia.
Operate for symptomatic disability, lens-induced disease, or to see the fundus.
Non-surgical: update glasses; mydriatic trial for PSC.

chunks.title: Subluxed / dislocated lens
chunks.tldr: Monocular diplopia, iridodonesis, phacodonesis, astigmatism, pupil block. Trauma commonest. Marfan: bilateral, up and out (superotemporal), AD, aortic root → echo. Homocystinuria: down and in, AR, learning difficulty, thromboembolism with anaesthesia → B6, methionine-restricted diet. Weill–Marchesani: microspherophakia, short stature/fingers → lens into AC, reverse pupil block. Also PXF, syphilis, Ehlers–Danlos, sulfite oxidase.
points: Lens in AC: dilate, lie supine, push back → pilocarpine + PI; or remove.
Lens in vitreous: observe if capsule intact and quiet; PPV lensectomy if inflamed.
Subluxation: observe/refract (prevent amblyopia in kids); remove if diplopia/unstable refraction.
Check syphilis serology.
chunks.hook: Marfan looks Up (superotemporal); Homocystinuria Heads Home Down (inferonasal).

chunks.title: Pregnancy & Lyme disease
chunks.tldr: Pregnancy: corneal thickening/curvature change, contact lens intolerance → don't prescribe new glasses until weeks postpartum; delay refractive surgery ≥3 months after pregnancy/nursing. Preeclampsia (>20 weeks): arteriolar spasm, serous RDs (1% preeclampsia, 10% eclampsia), PRES (cortical blindness, brisk pupils) → BP control, delivery. Hypercoagulable (RVO, DIC); meningioma growth; worse DR, CSCR, IIH. Lyme: conjunctivitis commonest, VII palsy, uveitis, optic neuritis; ELISA → Western blot; doxycycline 100 mg bd 10–21 d (amoxicillin in kids/pregnancy); neuro-ophthalmic → IV ceftriaxone 2 g.
points: Headache in pregnancy → BP, fields, discs; MRI/MRV if venous thrombosis suspected.
Drops in pregnancy: punctal occlusion.

cards.q: Treatment for Lyme disease with neuro-ophthalmic involvement?
cards.a: IV ceftriaxone 2 g daily for 2–3 weeks.

chunks.title: Convergence insufficiency & accommodative spasm
chunks.tldr: CI: young adults, near discomfort; exophoria at near, remote NPC (>8 cm), low base-out fusional amplitudes (break 10–15 Δ). 4 Δ base-in clears print in CI, blurs in accommodative insufficiency. Rx: correct refraction, pencil push-ups (± 6 Δ BO), orthoptic vision therapy (best in kids), base-in reading prism. Convergence paralysis (acute) → image. Accommodative spasm: stressed teens, fluctuating myopia (up to 10 D) that vanishes with cycloplegia, miosis; counsel, near add, cycloplegia if resistant.
points: Spasm of near reflex mimics VI palsy — look for miosis.
Pseudomyopia: hyperglycaemia, sulfa drugs, anticholinesterases.

chunks.title: SJS / TEN
chunks.tldr: EM (target lesions, usually HSV/Mycoplasma) is separate from SJS/TEN (mostly drugs: sulfonamides, anticonvulsants, allopurinol, NSAIDs; first 2 months). SJS <10% BSA, overlap 10–30%, TEN >30%. Genetics: HLA-B*15:02 + carbamazepine (Asians), HLA-B*58:01 + allopurinol. Eye: pseudomembranous conjunctivitis, lid margin ulcers → later symblepharon, trichiasis, dry eye, LSCD. Rx: stop drug, burn unit; daily fornix sweep, topical steroid, lubricants, antibiotics if defects; amniotic membrane over lid margins/fornices within 72 h.
points: Mortality: SJS 1–5%, TEN 25–35%.
Late: epilation, entropion repair with buccal graft, KPro (guarded).
chunks.hook: SJS eyes: membrane early (AMT in 72 h) saves the surface.

cards.q: HLA allele linking carbamazepine to SJS in Asians?

chunks.title: Vitamin A deficiency, albinism, Wilson
chunks.tldr: Vitamin A: night blindness first, Bitot spots (X1B), corneal xerosis → keratomalacia (often after measles); WHO XN–XF. Rx: 200,000 IU days 1, 2 and 2 weeks (100,000 if <1 yr; lower in women of childbearing age). Albinism: VA 20/40–20/400, nystagmus, TIDs, foveal hypoplasia, misrouted chiasm; OCA (AR, tyrosinase), ocular (XL; carriers mud-splattered fundus). Hermansky–Pudlak (bleeding; Puerto Rico) and Chédiak–Higashi (infections). Wilson: Kayser–Fleischer ring (Descemet copper, starts superiorly, gonio), sunflower cataract; ↓ceruloplasmin; ring fades with treatment.
points: Secondary vitamin A deficiency: bariatric surgery, IBD, CF, liver disease.
Albinism: check platelets before surgery.
Arcus in <40 → fasting lipids.
chunks.hook: Wilson: copper ring on Descemet, sunflower on the lens.

cards.q: WHO dose of vitamin A for xerophthalmia in a child >1 year?
cards.a: 200,000 IU on days 1 and 2, repeated at 2 weeks.

chunks.title: Hypotony & the blind painful eye
chunks.tldr: Hypotony (≤5 mm Hg) → folds, maculopathy, choroidals, flat AC. Causes: wound/bleb leak (Seidel), overfiltration, cyclodialysis cleft, scleral perforation, uveitis, RD, oral CAI + β-blocker, cidofovir, systemic (dehydration, uraemia, myotonic). Fix the cause; drain choroidals if kissing, lens–cornea touch (emergency) or decompensation. Blind painful eye: find the cause — epithelial defect, uveitis, high IOP, hypotony; B-scan if no view (tumour). Rx: atropine + steroid, lubrication/tarsorrhaphy, IOP drops, cyclophotocoagulation, retrobulbar alcohol/chlorpromazine, enucleation/evisceration (not if tumour possible).
points: Low IOP alone with good vision and formed AC can be watched.
Monocular patients: polycarbonate glasses always.
Periodic B-scan (~3-yearly) in blind eyes without fundus view.
chunks.hook: Blind + painful: atropine and steroid first; scan for tumour before evisceration.

cards.q: Contraindication to evisceration of a blind painful eye?

chunks.title: NF1 & NF2
chunks.tldr: NF1 (17q, AD): ≥2 of ≥6 café-au-lait, neurofibromas (1 plexiform or ≥2), axillary freckling, optic pathway glioma (12–15%), ≥2 Lisch nodules (~10% × age; 98% after puberty), sphenoid/tibial dysplasia, affected relative. Eye: plexiform neurofibroma (S-shaped lid) → glaucoma, pulsatile proptosis (absent sphenoid wing), choroidal nodules on NIR-OCT. Exam yearly to age 6, then 2-yearly; MRI only if signs. NF2 (22q): bilateral acoustic neuromas, juvenile PSC cataract, combined hamartoma, ERM, ONSM.
points: Watch for amblyopia from ptotic plexiform lid.

cards.a: Juvenile posterior subcapsular cataract (also combined hamartoma, ERM).

chunks.title: Sturge–Weber, TSC, VHL, Wyburn–Mason, AT
chunks.tldr: Sturge–Weber (GNAQ somatic): port-wine stain (V1/V2), glaucoma (early = goniodysgenesis; late = ↑episcleral venous pressure), diffuse choroidal haemangioma ('tomato ketchup'), leptomeningeal angioma, seizures; avoid α-agonists if brain involved. TSC: retinal astrocytic hamartoma (mulberry, calcifies), adenoma sebaceum, ash-leaf spots, seizures, renal angiomyolipoma, cardiac rhabdomyoma. VHL (3p): retinal haemangioblastoma with feeder vessels, cerebellar haemangioblastoma, RCC, phaeochromocytoma → laser/cryo; screen BP, catecholamines, MRI, abdominal US. Wyburn–Mason: racemose AV malformation + midbrain AVM (no Rx; dental bleeding risk). Ataxia-telangiectasia: conjunctival telangiectasia, oculomotor apraxia, infections, leukaemia, radiosensitivity.
points: Multiple/bilateral retinal haemangioblastomas = VHL.
Choroidal haemangioma with SRF: PDT or low-dose plaque.
Astrocytoma DDx: retinoblastoma.
chunks.hook: VHL: Very Hungry Lesions (feeders) + kidney and adrenal tumours.
